messages:
Lara Chen: thinking out loud — our spot queue for eu-west-1 is getting fragmented. mixing H100s + A10gs + a few cheaper gpus to hit cost targets, but binpacking is leaving tiny unusable leftovers and causing higher pod startup failures this week. anyone seen a neat trick to reduce fragmentation without blowing up latency?
Mike Ortiz: we saw that last month. main wins were 1) prefer node types by shape (vram/SM) for particular workloads, 2) introduce lightweight binpacking tiers for low-cost jobs so they don't pollute the main pool.
Sanjay Patel: agree re tiers. Another lever: shorten binpack window so we don't keep tiny holes for long. also use pod anti-affinity only when needed — it increases fragmentation.
Aliyah Gomez: can we do a fast fallback lane on eviction instead of waiting for reprovisioning? like immediately route the in-flight requests to a smaller model variant running in on-demand or lower-tier preemptible. switching should be transparent at the proxy layer.
Lara Chen: yes fallback lanes + model variants is in the roadmap (optimize does suggestions) but we need the control-plane hooks to detect an eviction within ~200ms and signal fallback. deploy-bot: Spot instance interruption notice received for i-0a1b2c3d (A10G)  — 2 min warning.
Mike Ortiz: that's the problem — the cloud notice latency is inconsistent. sometimes we get <2m, sometimes nothing. For quick recovery we should: checkpoint KV cache continuously to s3 and switch to KV-less mode briefly. that costs tokens but keeps latency bounded.
Sanjay Patel: checkpointing every n tokens works, but cost. alternative: keep a tiny warm pool of low-cost on-demand or dedicated micro capacity in every AZ to absorb evictions for 30s while we reschedule. size could be adaptive based on recent eviction rate.
Aliyah Gomez: question: are we packing different sequence length distributions on same machines? mixing long-context and short-context jobs on same instance worsens throughput predictability — pack by seqlen ranges to reduce kernel variance.
Lara Chen: good call — add seqlen bin to scheduler signals. also can we try cross-AZ fallback instead of cross-type when a whole instance family is scarce? cross-AZ adds latency though.
Mike Ortiz: we simulated three configs: (A) hetero-mix with per-AZ preference, (B) iso-family packing with cross-AZ fallback, (C) tiny warm on-demand pool + hetero spot. C had the best p99 tail but +8% cost vs pure-spot. tradeoff seems acceptable for critical SLAs.
Sanjay Patel: small config snippet we used for binpack weights:```json
{"weights":{"A100":1.0,"H100":0.9,"A10G":0.6,"RTX6000":0.4},"pack_horizon_secs":90,"min_warm_on_demand":3}
```
Aliyah Gomez: +1 to pack_horizon tuning. Also we should prefer instance types with predictable preemption correlation — avoiding families that share underlying hardware pools across AZs.
Lara Chen: ops ask: how do we present this to product when we propose the 8% cost bump for better p99? need clear numbers: p99 improvement, expected success-rate on evictions, and SRE ops overhead.
Mike Ortiz: draft numbers from sim: p99 latency down from 1100ms -> 420ms, cold-failure rate down 5.2% -> 0.9%, additional infra spend +7.8% overall. I'll push the simulation results to the shared drive.
Sanjay Patel: implementation plan: 1) add seqlen and family hint to scheduler 2) adaptive warm pool controller 3) fast eviction webhooks + model-variant routing 4) KV checkpoint policy toggle per route. can take 3 sprints with 1 engineer each + oncall testing.
Aliyah Gomez: I'll start a small canary: enable warm pool in eu-west-1 with min_warm_on_demand=2 and pack_horizon_secs=60 for low-priority batch to validate fragmentation changes.
Lara Chen: perfect. create a short playbook for oncall: how to eyeball eviction cascades and when to increase warm pool. include runbook commands.
deploy-bot: Canary started: warm-pool-eu-west1 (2 nodes) — status: provisioning.
Mike Ortiz: ping me when canary metrics are available (cpu/gpu-util, p99, eviction count). I'll put up a dashboard.
Lara Chen: thanks all — will follow up next week with canary metrics and a short summary for product. :shipit:
